site.title: THE REMAINED
site.description:
**Those who never left.**
A serialized record of altered continuation.

body: the city stayed open

not because nothing changed

*but because change didn’t require collapse*

posts.title: plain orientation
body:
people kept calling it an “infection”
because that’s the word they had

**it never behaved like one**

no spread. no wave. no outbreak.
just a change that stayed put.

posts.title: rule, clear and calm
body:
**it doesn’t pass between people**

no one is “exposed” by sitting nearby
or sharing a cup
or touching a doorknob

if you’re searching for the moment it started
there often isn’t one

rooms feel different now
not because of danger
but because bodies move through them differently

posts.title: expectations
body:
> *yes, i pause a lot.
yes, i tilt my head.
yes, i listen before i move.*

*no, i’m not waiting for prey.*

*i’m waiting for the room to finish loading.*

posts.title: “clicking”
body:
people expect sounds.
clicking. tapping. something cinematic.

there isn’t any.

my part is quiet.
the world does the talking.

posts.title: genre
body:
*if you’ve watched too many movies,
this probably looks familiar.*

*the difference is:*

*nothing here is deteriorating.
nothing is spreading.
nothing is hunting you*

posts.title: eyes
body:
my eyes aren’t gone.
they’re… reassigned.
light is optional now.
accuracy isn’t.

posts.title: what it does
body:
**it doesn’t heal what’s damaged**

it builds a workaround

function continues
the original damage stays

posts.title: personal draft
body:
**[DRAFT] [UNSENT] [AUTHOR REDACTED]**

**i’m okay
i’m not “better”
i’m just less stranded inside my own day**

**[DRAFT DELETED]**
[SENT: “doing fine, thanks”]

> “bought long sleeves in july

not for warmth
for fewer questions.”

posts.title: explanation fatigue
body:
*the old tools were visible.
canes. braces. devices.*

*this one isn’t.*

*which means people keep trying to guess.
and i keep pretending i don’t notice.*

it didn’t give me “vision”
it gave me navigation
i can find the hallway without counting the steps now

posts.title: outcomes, demystified
body:
**outcomes were ordinary:**

some improved.
some stabilized.
some declined anyways.

none of it was called a miracle.
it was all logged like weather.

**log:**
week 12 - stable
week 20 - stable
week 31 - stable
week 44 - stable
week 58 - stable
> *the strange part is how long “stable” can last*

posts.title: reminder to self:
body:
> *don’t schedule anything important
right after fluorescent lighting*

*i forget every time
i pay for it every time*

posts.title: closing
body:
there is no final stage

no “turning”
no outbreak
no cure

just life continuing under adjusted conditions
and the slow work of making that livable

yes, it looks like mold in certain lighting.

no, i’m not “turning.”

**i am, unfortunately, still paying rent.**

*someone called it a “bloater” arm.*

*rude.*

*it’s not bloated. it’s reinforced.*

*also it lets me carry all the groceries in one trip again, so who’s winning.*

moss spots show up in joints.
along scar tissue.
where friction used to win.

people see the dark patches and think “infection.”

it’s closer to heat map.

strain leaves color.

the shedding freaks people out.

it’s maintenance.

like replacing worn layers after a hard week.

i thought it meant something was wrong.

turns out it meant something was compensating.

that’s a very different diagnosis.

*the texture is actually more like cork.*

*it shows up where skin used to tear.*

*ugly, yes.
but it works.*

people keep asking if it hurts.

no.

what hurts is watching them decide whether to stand closer or farther away.

most people breathe it in and nothing happens.

it needs a niche.

scars. inflammation. old damage.

it’s an opportunist, not a predator.

the closest thing to an “outbreak” happened in spring.

pollen. fog. allergies.

boring ecology.

that’s the point.

if it wanted apocalypse, it would act like one.

it doesn’t.

it wants hosts who keep walking around.

posts.title: etiquette shift
body:
people used to say
*“will it go away?”*

now they ask
*“what do you need?”*

that’s the adjustment.
less curiosity, more accommodation

posts.title: clarification
body:
this isn’t a loss of humanity.

it’s a different prioritization.

rooms before faces.
paths before expressions.

i still recognize people.
i just don’t need to look at them first.
